ui.label: Test type
ui.help: Which test to run. IPTV test: pick the receivers in the device rows, a PC and up to three tablets on its USB, on the same or different TV channels.

ui.label: Devices
ui.help: The PCs and tablets in this test, found by themselves. Tick the ones to use.

ui.label: Video quality
ui.help: Video quality the sender sends. Example: UHD · 3840×2160 · 35 Mbps.

ui.label: Channel per device
ui.help: The TV channel each receiver watches. Default: a different channel each (CH1, CH2, CH3).

ui.label: Duration
ui.help: How long to measure. Example: 100h. The test ends by itself after it.

ui.label: Send quality reports
ui.help: Receivers send 1-second values while testing.
ui.available: Always on in this build (Off comes later)

ui.label: Transport
ui.help: How the video is carried. Default RTP / MPEG-TS (most IPTV services).

ui.label: Bitrate
ui.help: Video bitrate of the chosen quality. Example: UHD 35 Mbps. Higher loads the router more.

ui.label: Sender mode
ui.help: Send prepared files (default, light on the PC) or encode live.

ui.label: Broadcast
ui.help: Send only during a test (default), or all the time: Always-on keeps the TV channels on air after Stop, like an ISP. Stop it with Stop broadcast.

ui.label: Multicast groups · port
ui.help: Channel addresses and port. Default 239.1.1.1~3 : 5004. Change only when your network needs it.
ui.available: Set in the plan file in this build

ui.label: TTL
ui.help: Hops a video packet may pass. Default 16. Lower values may be dropped by the router in NAT mode.

ui.label: DSCP
ui.help: Priority mark on video packets. Default 0.

ui.label: Hole-punch mode (no-IGMP firmware)
ui.help: Primed unicast for development/SDK routers without IGMP. Auto finds out by itself.

ui.label: Channel change
ui.help: Change TV channels by itself every N minutes (CH1 -> CH2 -> CH3 -> CH1). All three channels are sent. Any N from 1 to 120 works from the CLI.

ui.label: Stagger channel changes
ui.help: Change receivers one after another, 10 s apart (Off: all at once). 5 to 60 s works from the CLI.

ui.label: Jitter warning level
ui.help: Jitter above this turns a box yellow. Default 50 ms. The fail limit (150 ms) never changes.

ui.label: Reorder window
ui.help: Out-of-order packets sorted within this time are not errors. Default 1,000 ms.
ui.available: Fixed at 1,000 ms in this build

ui.label: Player buffer
ui.help: How much video the player keeps ahead. Default 1,000 ms.

ui.label: PC player
ui.help: The player on the receiver PC. Default mpv (hardware decoding; VLC 3 decodes UHD HEVC in software and can fall behind).

ui.label: Receive buffer size
ui.help: Socket buffer of the receiver. Default 16 MB.
ui.available: Fixed at 16 MB in this build

ui.label: Start-up wait (warm-up max)
ui.help: Longest wait for a steady stream before measuring. Default 15 s.

ui.label: Packet capture
ui.help: Keep a packet capture of the test.

ui.label: Evidence capture
ui.help: Also keep a picture of each trouble second: the video this PC received, rendered from 1 s before to 3 s after (4 frames a second). The packets of each trouble (a pcap, 10 s before to 5 s after) are always kept. On by default (2026-10-10): engineers believe what they see.

ui.label: Channel change success timeout
ui.help: Longest time a channel change may take to count as a success.

ui.label: Source video
ui.help: Video to send on each TV channel: Generated (default) or a movie from the sender PC's Videos folder. Example: CH1 = movie.mp4.

ui.label: Source length
ui.help: How much of a picked movie is made for sending, once, then reused: its first 10 minutes (fast, small, loops every 10 min) or the whole movie (hours to make, several GB).

ui.label: PC playback (PC receiver only)
ui.help: Play the video on the receiver PC. Off = analyze only (playback NOT RUN).

ui.label: Player window size (PC receiver only)
ui.help: Size of the player window. Hardly changes the decoding load.
